questions.q: Goose pins its feature resolver in the workspace manifest. What does `resolver = "2"` do in the root Cargo.toml?
options: Allows two versions of every dependency in one graph
Enables edition-2021 feature unification: dev-dependency features do not leak into the normal build
Compiles the workspace twice in parallel
Forces every crate onto one edition
explanation: The resolver never splits a semver range into two versions in one build.
Nothing compiles twice; the field only selects the feature resolver algorithm.
Editions are per-crate settings, unrelated to the resolver field.

questions.q: A fn takes `prompt: String`, then the caller uses `prompt` again. The compiler error is caused by:
options: Ownership moved into the fn; the caller no longer owns the value
explanation: Borrow checking rejects moves, it never hoards.
String is sized; the error is about ownership transfer.
The parameter need not be `mut`; the value would still be moved.

questions.q: Which signature is both valid and allocation-free for trimming a prompt slice?
explanation: Taking String by value forces a move and a new allocation.
&mut str is needlessly mutable and still allocates a String.
'static lifetimes do not fit borrowed input slices.

questions.q: `fn longest(a: &str, b: &str) -> &str` fails to compile because:
options: The compiler cannot choose the returned lifetime - you must tie it to the inputs with explicit lifetimes like <'a>
explanation: Multiple refs are fine; elision just cannot cover two inputs.
Copy-ness is unrelated to lifetime elision rules.
Returning a borrowed slice is fine when lifetimes are annotated.

questions.q: You add a field to a serde struct that old config files never set. Which attribute keeps deserialization working?
explanation: skip would drop the field entirely, not default it.
rename_all only changes naming style.
flatten inlines a nested map; it does not default missing fields.

questions.q: Inside `fn load() -> anyhow::Result<Config>`, the statement `let cfg = parse()?;` does:
options: Returns Err early from load(), converting the error into the outer type
Logs and continues with a default
explanation: `?` never panics; panics use unwrap/expect.
There is no built-in retry behavior in the operator.
The operator unwraps to the value or returns - it never skips.

questions.q: The Provider MessageStream is `Pin<Box<dyn Stream<...>>>`. Why must the future/stream be Pinned?
options: Async state machines may be self-referential and must not move in memory
explanation: Pin is about movement semantics, not box transparency.
Items pass plainly through the stream; no encryption involved.
Logging is unrelated to pinning.

questions.q: Shared mutable state across tokio tasks is typically `Arc<Mutex<T>>` because:
options: Arc makes owners, Mutex makes exclusive access - together: shared ownership + safe mutation
It is faster than plain T
explanation: Arc only shares ownership; mutation needs synchronization.
Mutex only synchronizes; something must own the value across tasks.
The pair costs more than unsynchronized access - safety, not speed.

questions.q: The AGENTS.md convention for goose library fallible functions is:
explanation: Panics are for unrecoverable states, not routine errors.
Numeric codes hide error context.
unwrap chains are precisely what the convention replaces.

questions.q: `String::from("prompt")` differs from `&*"prompt"`-style usage because:
options: String is on the heap and owned; &str is a view, often static
explanation: &str is a borrowed view, frequently into static memory.
String is growable/mutable by design.
They are different types that reference each other.

questions.q: Why do `goose-sdk-types` / `goose-provider-types` exist as separate type-only crates?
options: To make the workspace compile faster by hiding code
Extension authors can compile against contract types without depending on the whole agent engine
They hold binaries for each OS
They duplicate the engine types for CI
explanation: They do not hide code; they hold shared contract types.
There are no binaries inside the type crates.
They are the canonical types, not duplicates.

questions.q: In the message data model, `MessageContentBlock` exists so:
options: Content mixes text, tool calls, thinking, and errors in one typed sequence the loop can dispatch on
Messages can be compressed as one string
explanation: The enum replaces string-bashing; blocks remain typed.
Providers consume these same blocks.
Text is only one variant among many.

questions.q: Changing a key inside `config.yaml` (e.g. an extension entry) takes effect in goose because:
options: Config::global() reads the file and typed getters feed runtime construction - new sessions re-read it
explanation: No watcher exists; reading happens at config access.
Compilation is not involved.
Reinstall is not needed; new sessions pick up the file.

questions.q: The AGENTS.md parity rule for the agent loop requires:
options: Every change must preserve behavior across both legacy and state-machine paths with tests
explanation: Legacy stays until parity is complete.
Both paths ship and must agree.
Formal fuzzing is not the rule; behavior tests are.

questions.q: In the state machine (ops_*/effects), operations and effects are separated so:
options: Ops are pure descriptions; effects apply them - making transitions testable and traceable
Each runs on its own thread
Ops can be skipped in dev
explanation: Threading is an implementation detail, not the split's purpose.
Effects are the actual side effects of running ops.
Ops always run; the split keeps them observable.

questions.q: Per the Provider trait, the one method every provider MUST implement is:
explanation: complete() derives from stream().
fetch_supported_models defaults to an empty list.
retry_config defaults to RetryConfig::default().

questions.q: When a user denies a tool call in the confirmation flow, the agent receives:
options: The tool result with is_error and a denial message so it can course-correct
A retry of the same call
explanation: Silent ends would hide policy from the model.
Denied calls are not auto-retried.
Records are internal; the agent gets a proper result.

questions.q: `ToolPermissionRecord` hashes the call context instead of only the tool name to:
options: Scope remembered approvals to the same arguments/context, not the whole tool
explanation: Names remain readable in records.
Size is not the goal.
Hashing aids scoped matching, not sorting.

questions.q: Schema normalization on the MCP boundary solves the problem of:
options: Two servers exposing colliding tool names - they get namespaced before dispatch
explanation: Normalization is about naming/schemas, not process speed.
Token limits are a separate subsystem.
OAuth is orthogonal to schema handling.

questions.q: Which pair is the observability stack goose uses per provider turn?
options: OpenTelemetry gen_ai spans (usage/error attributes) plus RUST_LOG-scoped tracing
explanation: println is explicitly not production observability.
Spans export via otel; RUST_LOG controls noise.
Perf counters are not the tracing story.

questions.q: An issue labeled Ready in goose means:
options: Any contributor may claim and implement it - it is triaged, scoped, and unblocked
explanation: Closed issues are done, not Ready.
Needs-design items are not Ready.
Meta issues are a separate bucket.

questions.q: The first step of reproducing a reported bug is:
options: Read the issue fully, then script the minimal repro steps against the pinned checkout
explanation: Fixing before reproducing gambles.
Rebase is unrelated to repro.
Design docs apply to features, not repros.

questions.q: `git bisect run <script>` works because:
options: The script returns the first bad commit
The script's exit code (0/125/other) tells git whether the commit is good, unbuildable, or bad
Git reads the script's stdout commit hash
explanation: No scoreboard exists.
Bisect computes the first bad commit from exit codes.
The exit code is the signal, not stdout.

questions.q: After intentionally changing behavior, a snapshot test file is updated by:
options: Running the snapshot update command, then reviewing the diff before committing
explanation: Blind updates hide regressions.
Deleting the snapshot removes the guard entirely.
Commented assertions are disabled guards.

questions.q: Goose's test provider records calls into a JSON file whose keys are:
options: SHA-256 hashes of the stabilized input messages
explanation: Indeterminate keys would break replay.
Line numbers are irrelevant at runtime.
Provider names do not distinguish inputs.

questions.q: `just record-mcp-tests` captures:
options: Real MCP server traffic as recorded fixtures for deterministic tests
explanation: Recording is the point - mocks are the replay half.
It records full interactions, not just errors.
There is no video capture.

questions.q: Clippy runs in the workspace with `-D warnings`, which means:
options: Any clippy warning fails the build
explanation: Volume is unchanged; the lint level changes.
Lints are promoted to errors, never silenced.
Clippy runs on the whole crate, warning-free required.

questions.q: To fix the same bug in both legacy and state-machine agent paths, you must:
options: Fix whichever path a reviewer prefers
Apply the fix to both paths and add a regression test proving identical behavior
Fix state machine only, legacy is deprecated
Add a feature flag per path
explanation: Parity is a hard rule, not reviewer preference.
Both paths ship until parity completes.
Flags do not create behavioral agreement.

questions.q: The correct order for a bugfix PR is:
options: Write a failing regression test that captures the bug -> make it pass -> keep the test
explanation: Without the test the bug can silently return.
Post-merge tests never guard the PR itself.
Automated regression tests are the convention here.

questions.q: `deny.toml` guards the workspace by:
options: Enforcing allowed licenses and banned dependency versions/duplicates
Deleting failing crates at build time
explanation: unsafe is not enforced by cargo-deny
It flags crates rather than deleting them.
It audits the graph, not the network.

questions.q: `ExtensionConfig` is modeled as:
options: A loose map of untyped YAML
A serde-tagged enum (stdio / builtin / platform / streamable_http) dispatched on the `type` field
A single struct with optional everything
explanation: The variants give each surface its own validated shape.
One struct with all-optional fields would fail validation silently.
It is the config.yaml extension surface.

questions.q: Which plugin name passes the enforce rule of `validate_plugin_name`?
explanation: Uppercase fails the lowercase-only rule.
Names must start with a letter or digit.
Consecutive dots are banned.

questions.q: `discover_enabled_plugins` looks at which roots?
options: The user plugins dir plus the project .agents/plugins dir, filtered by settings files
explanation: CWD alone would miss user-scoped plugins.
There is no remote registry in v1.49.0 discovery.
The OS registry is irrelevant.

questions.q: The OSV malware check blocks a package only when:
options: The package is written in Rust
OSV returns a MAL-* advisory; network failures fail open
The package is older than a year
explanation: Language is irrelevant to advisory checks.
Age is not a signal.
There is no binary scanning; only advisory lookup.

questions.q: What does the default `complete()` in the Provider trait do?
options: Calls stream() then collect_stream() into one (Message, ProviderUsage)
Returns the system prompt as the answer
explanation: HTTP is a provider-specific concern below the trait.
Retry is a separate trait/config concern.
complete delegates to the stream contract.

questions.q: In `collect_stream`, consecutive text deltas are:
options: Coalesced into one growing text block, and usage kept from the last chunk
Each wrapped in a new message sent to the user
explanation: Partial text is expected, not an error.
One message with one text block is the aggregation contract.
Compression is not part of the API.

questions.q: `ensure_usage_tokens` estimates counts only when:
options: Input or output counts are missing, and prefers vendor numbers whenever present
explanation: Billing status is irrelevant to estimation policy.
Estimation is the universal fallback, not local-only.
Duration is not a trigger.

questions.q: OpenAI tool-call arguments arrive as a JSON string, and the mapper:
options: Stores them verbatim as text content
Parses that string and builds a `ToolRequest` with structured arguments
explanation: Text content would break tool dispatch.
Strings are the required wire form.
Arguments are plain JSON strings, not base64.

questions.q: The OAuth endpoint transport policy in goose is:
options: Any HTTPS or HTTP endpoint is fine
HTTPS always, HTTP only for loopback addresses
explanation: Plain HTTP for remote endpoints would expose codes.
HTTP-only would forbid secure vendors.
OAuth uses HTTPS endpoints, not websockets.

questions.q: Your MCP tool rejects an empty note with `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The maintainer-correct code is:
options: Keep it - all rejections are internal
Use `INVALID_PARAMS` because the caller sent an unacceptable value; reserve `INTERNAL_ERROR` for your own faults
explanation: Conflating caller faults with server faults misleads the agent.
Error codes are required metadata.
A bad value is not a timeout.

miniLab.title: Capstone green: ship your production-grade extension
miniLab.instructions:
Final capstone. Deliver a complete, documented, tested extension that solves a real workflow you have.

1. Create the extension directory (Cargo.toml for a server/provider, or plugin.json for a plugin) with src/ (or commands/ + skills/), tests/, README.md, and docs/design.md that states the problem and the security model.
2. Run the quality gates and record them: `cargo fmt` output, `cargo test` (capture the `test result:` line), and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, appending everything to qa-report.txt with a final marker line CLIPPY-RUN-DONE (plugin route: record your validation outputs and a final GATES-RUN-DONE line instead).
3. Fix every clippy warning - do not use #[allow(...)] to hide them.
4. Use the extension for one real live session and save the transcript to demo.md (what you asked, what tool/command fired, the result).
5. Run the provided verify script below and paste its full output. The auto-grading verdict passes only when the output contains every string in passMarkers.
